### CVB Financial Corp. Reports Earnings for the Third Quarter 2026


**Third Quarter 2026**


- **Net earnings of $78.1 million, or $0.44 per share**
- **Net interest margin expanded to 3.89%**
- **Return on average assets (“ROAA”) of 1.48%**
- **R** **eturn on average tangible common equity (“ROATCE”)1 of 16.22%**


Ontario, CA, Oct. 21, 2026 – CVB Financial Corp. (NASDAQ: CVBF) (“CVBF” or the “Company”) and its subsidiary, Citizens Business Bank, National Association (“Citizens” or the “Bank”), announced earnings for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.


CVB Financial Corp. reported net income of $78.1 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared with $48.3 million for the second quarter of 2026 and $52.6 million for the third quarter of 2025. Diluted earnings per share were $0.44 for the third quarter, compared to $0.29 for the prior quarter and $0.38 for the same period last year.


For the third quarter of 2026, annualized return on average equity (“ROAE”) was 9.70%, annualized ROATCE1 was 16.22%, and annualized ROAA was 1.48%.


David Brager, Chief Executive Officer of the Company, commented, “Our third-quarter results reflect solid financial performance, increased profitability, net interest margin expansion and disciplined expense management following the Heritage Bank of Commerce acquisition. The third quarter represented our 198th consecutive quarter of profitability. We remain focused on the integration, serving our customers and supporting our communities and associates as we extend our relationship-focused banking model across California’s major economic centers. We are grateful for the continued trust of our customers and the dedication of our associates.”


1 Non-U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (“GAAP”) financial measures. See GAAP to non–GAAP reconciliations of the measures are set forth at the last section of this press release.


**Highlights for the Third Quarter of 2026**


- Earnings per share growth of 15.8% from Q3 of 2025
- Net interest income increased $16.7 million, or 10.3% from Q2 of 2026
- Net interest margin increased 17 basis points to 3.89% from Q2 of 2026
- Adjusted ROAA of 1.59%2, excluding acquisition expense
- Adjusted ROATCE of 17.38%2, excluding acquisition expense
- Adjusted efficiency ratio2 of 42.10%, excluding acquisition expense
- Acquisition related expenses declined to $8.1 million, compared with $31.4 million for Q2 of 2026
- Loans increased $105.0 million, or 0.87% from the end of Q2 of 2026
- Average loans increased by $476.7 million, 4.13% from Q2 2026
- Recapture of credit losses of $1.0 million, compared with provision for credit losses of $1 million in Q3 of 2025
- Average total deposit and customer repurchase agreements increased by $577.9 million, or 3.59% from Q2 of 2026
- Noninterest-bearing deposits represented 53.5% of total deposits at quarter end
- Repurchased $17.5 million of common stock during Q3 of 2026, bringing year-to-date repurchases to $22.6 million, or 1.0 million shares


2 Non-GAAP financial measures. See GAAP to non–GAAP reconciliations of the measures are set forth at the last section of this press release.


**INCOME STATEMENT HIGHLIGHTS**


**Net Interest Income**


Net interest income was $179.1 million for the third quarter of 2026, an increase of $16.7 million, or 10.25%, from the second quarter of 2026, and an increase of $63.5 million, or 54.93%, from the third quarter of 2025. The increases in net interest income compared to both periods largely reflect the full quarter impact of the Heritage acquisition, which closed on April 17, 2026. Interest income increased by $18.5 million, or 9.16%, from the second quarter of 2026, while interest expense increased by $1.9 million, or 4.71%, to $41.6 million in the third quarter of 2026. The quarter-over-quarter increase in net interest income was primarily due to a 17 basis point increase in tax equivalent net interest margin and a $891.9 million increase in average interest-earning assets.


Compared to the third quarter of 2025, the $63.5 million increase in net interest income was primarily attributable to a $70.5 million increase in interest income driven by a $4.58 billion increase in average interest-earning assets and a 47 basis point increase in the yield on average earning assets. The increase in interest income was offset by a $7.0 million increase in interest expense, primarily attributable to a $2.90 billion increase in average interest-bearing deposits and customer repurchase agreements.


**Net Interest Margin**


Our tax equivalent net interest margin was 3.89% for the third quarter of 2026, compared to 3.72% for the second quarter of 2026 and 3.33% for the third quarter of 2025. The 17 basis point increase in our net interest margin compared to the second quarter of 2026 was primarily attributable to a 16 basis points increase in our average interest-earning assets yield, driven by a 23 basis points increase in our average investment securities yield and a 13 basis points increase in our average loan yield. Discount accretion for acquired loans was approximately $3.3 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $3.0 million in the second quarter of 2026. The increase in investment securities yield reflected the Company’s post merger balance sheet optimization strategy, which included repositioning the investment portfolio acquired from Heritage as well as deploying the proceeds from the sale of Heritage’s mortgage loan pools into higher-yielding securities. The increase in average loan yields was primarily driven by the full quarter impact of the higher-yielding acquired assets, including $103.4 million of average factored receivables, which generated an average yield of 17.21% during the quarter. Cost of funds remained stable at 0.96% for the third quarter of 2026, as a four basis point decrease in our cost of deposits from 0.83% in the second quarter to 0.79% in the third quarter of 2026 was offset by increases in Federal Home Loan Bank (“FHLB”) borrowings and associated costs of cash flow hedges that hedged brokered time deposits in prior quarters.


Compared to the third quarter of 2025, tax equivalent net interest margin for the third quarter of 2026 increased by 56 basis points, reflecting a 47 basis point increase in the average interest-earning assets yield and a nine basis point decrease in cost of funds. The increase in earning assets yield was primarily due to a 41 basis point increase in average loan yields, due to continuing impact of originating new loans at higher yields compared to the lower yields on principal payments and payoffs of older loans and the impact from the loans acquired from Heritage. The average yield on investment securities increased by 31 basis points from the third quarter of 2025, despite the impact of $1.5 million reduction in interest income from the fair value hedges of our investment securities available-for-sale (“AFS”), which generated a negative carry during the third quarter of 2026 compared to the positive carry recognized in the same quarter last year. Partially offsetting these increases was a 75 basis point lower yield on funds deposited at the Federal Reserve, reflecting the impact of Federal Open Market Committee (“FOMC”) rate cuts during the latter part of 2025. The 25 basis point increase in the federal funds target rate at the end of the third quarter of 2026 had minimal impact on the third quarter’s interest income. Cost of funds decreased to 0.96% in the third quarter of 2026 from 1.05% in the third quarter of 2025. This decrease was driven by a 45 basis point reduction in cost of interest-bearing deposits and a 23 basis point decrease in cost of FHLB advances. Partially offsetting these lower funding costs, was a less favorable deposit mix, as noninterest-bearing deposits declined as a percentage of average total deposits to 52.6% in the third quarter of 2026 from 59.3% in the third quarter of 2025.


**Earning Assets and Deposits**


The increases in average earning assets and average total deposits were primarily attributable to the full quarter’s impact of the Heritage acquisition. On average, earning assets increased by $891.9 million compared to the second quarter of 2026 and increased $4.58 billion compared to the third quarter of 2025. The quarter-over-quarter increase in interest-earning assets was primarily attributable to a $489.6 million increase in investment securities, a $476.7 million increase in average loans, partially offset with a decrease of $77.9 million in average interest-earning deposits at the Federal Reserve. The increase from the third quarter of 2025 in interest-earning assets was primarily attributable to a $3.65 billion increase in average loans, a $924.6 million increase in average investment securities, partially offset by a $45.1 million decrease in average interest-earning deposits at the Federal Reserve.


The average balance on noninterest-bearing deposits increased by $330.6 million, or 4.07%, from the second quarter of 2026 and by $1.33 billion, or 18.68%, from the third quarter of 2025. The average balance on interest-bearing deposits and customer repurchase agreements increased $247.2 million from the second quarter of 2026 and $2.86 billion from the third quarter of 2025. On average, noninterest-bearing deposits were 52.6% of total deposits for the third quarter of 2026, compared to 52.3% for the second quarter of 2026 and 59.3% for the third quarter of 2025.


**SELECTED FINANCIAL HIGHLIGHTS**


**Provision for Credit Losses**


The Company recorded a $1.0 million recapture of credit losses in the third quarter of 2026, compared to no provision for credit losses in the second quarter of 2026 and $1.0 million provision for credit losses in the third quarter of 2025.


**Noninterest Income**


Noninterest income totaled $16.5 million for the third quarter of 2026, a decrease of $500,000 from $17.0 million for the second quarter of 2026 and an increase of $3.5 million from $13.0 million for the third quarter of 2025. The quarter-over-quarter decrease was primarily attributable to a $507,000 decrease in value of a CRA investment fund, a $359,000 decrease in trust and investment services income, and a $134,000 loss on the sale of two other real estate owned (“OREO”) properties, partially offset by a $580,000 increase in bank owned life insurance (“BOLI”) income and a $226,000 increase in service charges on deposit accounts. The year-over-year increase primarily reflected higher customer fee income and BOLI income resulting from the Heritage acquisition. Noninterest income in the third quarter of 2025 included $8.1 million in losses on the sale of AFS investments securities, partially offset by a $6.0 million legal settlement recorded in other income.


**Noninterest Expense**


Noninterest expense totaled $90.5 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $114.4 million for the second quarter of 2026 and $58.6 million for the third quarter of 2025. Acquisition related expenses associated with the Heritage merger totaled $8.1 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $31.4 million for the second quarter of 2026. Excluding acquisition related expense and the $4.3 million provision for unfunded loan commitments recorded in the second quarter, noninterest expense increased by $3.6 million from the second quarter of 2026. This increase was primarily driven by a full quarter of operating expenses associated with the Heritage acquisition.


As a percentage of average assets, noninterest expense was 1.71% for the third quarter of 2026, compared to 2.31% for the second quarter of 2026 and 1.50% for the third quarter of 2025. The efficiency ratio was 46.27% for the third quarter of 2026, compared to 63.75% for the second quarter of 2026 and 45.56% for the third quarter of 2025. Excluding acquisition related expenses and the provision for unfunded loan commitments, the adjusted efficiency ratio3 was 42.10% for the third quarter of 2026, compared to 43.88% for the second quarter of 2026 and 45.56% for the third quarter of 2025.


**Income Taxes**


Our effective tax rate for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 was 26.38%, compared with 25.81% for the second quarter of 2026 and 23.80% for the third quarter of 2025. Our estimated annual effective tax rate can vary depending upon the level of tax-advantaged income from municipal securities and BOLI, as well as tax credit investments.


3 Non-GAAP financial measures. See GAAP to non–GAAP reconciliations of the measures are set forth at the last section of this press release.


**BALANCE SHEET HIGHLIGHTS**


**Assets**


Total assets were $20.52 billion at September 30, 2026, a decrease of $660.5 million, or 3.12%, from $21.18 billion at June 30, 2026. The decrease was primarily attributable to a $815.8 million decrease in interest-earning balances due from the Federal Reserve, partially offset by a $105.0 million increase in total loans and a $46.8 million increase in investment securities.


Total assets increased by $4.89 billion, or 31.29%, from $15.63 billion at December 31, 2025. The increase in assets was primarily driven by an increase of $3.42 billion in total loans, a $769.7 million increase in investment securities, partially offset by a $174.9 million decrease in interest-earnings balances due from the Federal Reserve.


Compared to September 30, 2025, total assets increased by $4.86 billion, or 31.00%, from $15.67 billion. The increase in assets was primarily driven by an increase of $3.65 billion in total loans, an increase of $845.8 million in investment securities, offset by a decrease of $538.1 million in interest-earning balances due from the Federal Reserve.


The increases in total assets compared to December 31, 2025 and September 30, 2025 primarily reflect the impact of the Heritage acquisition completed on April 17, 2026, partially offset by balance sheet optimization activities during the second quarter of 2026.


**Investment Securities**


Total investment securities were $5.72 billion at September 30, 2026, an increase of $46.8 million, or 0.83%, from $5.68 billion at June 30, 2026, an increase of $769.7 million, or 15.54%, from December 31, 2025, and an increase of $845.8 million, or 17.34%, from $4.88 billion at September 30, 2025. The quarter-over-quarter increase in investment securities was primarily attributable to purchases of approximately $137.4 million of AFS securities and $6.2 million of held-to-maturity (“HTM”) securities.


The increase compared to December 31, 2025 and September 30, 2025 primarily reflected the result of the Heritage acquisition as well as the Company’s post merger balance sheet optimization strategy.


At September 30, 2026, HTM investment securities totaled $2.20 billion, a decrease of $23.2 million, or 1.05%, from June 30, 2026, a decrease of $75.1 million, or 3.31%, from December 31, 2025, and a decrease of $102.6 million, or 4.47%, from September 30, 2025.


At September 30, 2026, AFS investment securities totaled $3.53 billion, inclusive of a pre-tax net unrealized loss of $439.0 million. AFS securities increased $70.1 million, or 2.03%, from June 30, 2026, $844.8 million, or 31.48%, from December 31, 2025, and $948.4 million, or 36.77%, from September 30, 2025. The pre-tax net unrealized loss at September 30, 2026 increased $115.5 million from June 30, 2026, $131.2 million from December 31, 2025 and $105.2 million from September 30, 2025. The increase in net unrealized losses was primarily attributable to changes in market interest rates during the quarter.


**Loans**


Total loans and leases, at amortized cost, were $12.12 billion at September 30, 2026, an increase of $105.0 million, or 0.87%, from $12.02 billion at June 30, 2026. The quarter-over-quarter increase was primarily due to increases of $60.8 million in dairy & livestock and agribusiness loans, $48.8 million in commercial real estate loans, $28.7 million in Small Business Administration (“SBA”) loans, $19.1 million in construction loans, partially offset by decreases of $39.1 million in commercial and industrial loans, $9.1 million in consumer and other loans, $2.9 million in single-family residential (“SFR”) mortgage loans, and $2.3 million in municipal lease finance receivables.


Total loans and leases, at amortized cost, increased by $3.42 billion, or 39.35%, from December 31, 2025. The increase primarily reflected increases of $2.46 billion in commercial real estate loans, $466.2 million in commercial and industrial loans, $191.2 million in construction loans, $187.9 million in SBA loans, $157.6 million in consumer and other loans, and $56.6 million in SFR mortgage loans. These increases were partially offset by decreases of $89.8 million in dairy & livestock and agribusiness loans, and $5.7 million in municipal lease finance receivables loans.


Total loans and leases, at amortized cost, increased by $3.65 billion, or 43.10%, from September 30, 2025. The $3.65 billion increase included increases of $2.50 billion in commercial real estate loans, $500.7 million in commercial and industrial loans, $204.1 million in SBA loans, $199.1 million in construction loans, $156.3 million in consumer loans, $52.3 million in SFR mortgage loans, $48.8 million in dairy & livestock and agribusiness loans, partially offset by a decrease of $7.6 million in municipal lease finance receivables.


The increase in total loans and leases compared to December 31, 2025 and September 30, 2025 primarily reflected the Heritage acquisition, which added $3.10 billion of loans held for investment recorded at fair value on the acquisition date.


**Asset Quality**


During the third quarter of 2026, the Company recorded net charge-offs of $20,000, compared to $137,000 in the second quarter of 2026. The allowance for credit losses (“ACL”) totaled $125.6 million at September 30, 2026, compared to $126.7 million at June 30, 2026 and $79.3 million at September 30, 2025. The $46.3 million year-over-year increase primarily reflected the initial ACL of $46.6 million established for the purchased credit deteriorated (“PCD”) loans and purchased seasoned loans (“PSL”) acquired from the Heritage acquisition. At September 30, 2026, the ACL represented 1.04% of total loans and leases, compared to 1.05% at June 30, 2026 and 0.94% at September 30, 2025.


Nonperforming loans are defined as nonaccrual loans, including modified loans on nonaccrual, plus loans 90 days or more past due and still accruing interest. Nonperforming assets are defined as nonperforming loans plus OREO. Asset quality metrics are presented below.


The $2.1 million increase in nonperforming loans from June 30, 2026 was primarily due to the addition of two nonperforming SBA loans totaling $1.7 million, and one commercial and industrial loan of $985,000, partially offset by the payoffs and paydowns.


Classified loans are loans that are graded “substandard” or worse. Classified loans increased $4.2 million from June 30, 2026, primarily due to the downgrade of two nonperforming commercial real estate loans totaling $5.1 million and two commercial and industrial loans totaling $2.1 million, partially offset by upgrades, payoffs and paydowns. The year-over-year increase primarily reflected the addition of $30.8 million of classified loans acquired in the Heritage merger.


**Deposits & Customer Repurchase Agreements**


Deposits of $15.73 billion and customer repurchase agreements of $571.9 million totaled $16.30 billion at September 30, 2026, compared to $16.85 billion at June 30, 2026, $12.56 billion at December 31, 2025, and $12.58 billion at September 30, 2025. Deposits and customer repurchase agreements decreased $550.0 million, or 3.26%, from June 30, 2026, increased $3.74 billion, or 29.77% from December 31, 2025, and $3.73 billion, or 29.63%, from September 30, 2025. The increases from December 31, 2025 and September 30, 2025 primarily reflected $1.2 billion of noninterest-bearing deposits and $3.5 billion of interest-bearing deposits assumed in connection with the Heritage acquisition completed during the second quarter of 2026.


Noninterest-bearing deposits were $8.42 billion at September 30, 2026, a decrease of $190.6 million, or 2.21%, compared to $8.61 billion at June 30, 2026. Noninterest-bearing deposits increased $1.62 billion, or 23.76%, from $6.80 billion at December 31, 2025 and $1.17 billion, or 16.17%, from $7.24 billion at September 30, 2025. At September 30, 2026, noninterest-bearing deposits were 53.50% of total deposits, compared to 52.84% at June 30, 2026, 56.33% at December 31, 2025, and 59.76% at September 30, 2025. The decrease in the percentage of noninterest-bearing deposits from December 31, 2025 and September 30, 2025 primarily reflected the deposit mix acquired in the Heritage acquisition, which included a higher proportion of interest-bearing deposits.


**Borrowings**


As of September 30, 2026, total borrowings were $579.3 million, consisting of $540.0 million of FHLB advances and $39.3 million of subordinated debt assumed in the Heritage acquisition, compared to $539.0 million at June 30, 2026 and $500.0 million at December 31, 2025. At September 30, 2026, FHLB advances consisted of $300.0 million of 90 day advances hedged with cash flow hedges, under which the Company pays an average fixed rate of 4.22% and receives SOFR, a $200.0 million putable advance at a rate of 4.27% maturing in May 2027, and a $40.0 million overnight advance at a rate of 4.36%, which matured on October 1, 2026.


**Capital**


The Company’s total equity was $3.13 billion at September 30, 2026, compared to $2.30 billion at December 31, 2025 and $2.28 billion at September 30, 2025. The increase of $835.1 million from December 31, 2025 was primarily due to $840.2 million of common shares issued in connection with the Heritage acquisition in the second quarter of 2026 and $177.4 million in net earnings, partially offset by $97.8 million in cash dividends declared and $22.7 million related to common stock repurchases. During the first nine months of 2026, the Company purchased approximately 1.0 million shares under the 2026 Repurchase Program, at an average price of $22.22 per share for an aggregate purchase price of $22.6 million, including $17.5 million repurchased during the third quarter of 2026.


Our tangible book value per share was $10.92 at September 30, 2026, compared to $11.07 at June 30, 2026, $11.24 at December 31, 2025 and $10.98 at September 30, 2025, respectively.


Our capital ratios remained well above applicable regulatory capital requirements.


**CitizensTrust**


As of September 30, 2026, CitizensTrust had approximately $4.94 billion in assets under management and administration, including $3.81 billion in assets under management. Revenues were $3.8 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $4.2 million for the second quarter of 2026 and $3.9 million for the third quarter of 2025. CitizensTrust provides trust, investment and brokerage related services, as well as financial, estate and business succession planning.


**Corporate Overview**


CVB Financial Corp. (“CVBF”) is the holding company for Citizens Business Bank, National Association. CVBF is one of the ten largest bank holding companies headquartered in California with more than $20 billion in total assets as of the closing of the mergers with Heritage Commerce Corp and its principal banking subsidiary, Heritage Bank of Commerce. Citizens Business Bank, National Association, is consistently recognized as one of the top performing banks in the nation and offers a wide array of banking, lending and investing services with more than 75 banking centers and three trust office locations serving California.


Shares of CVB Financial Corp. common stock are listed on the NASDAQ under the ticker symbol “CVBF”. For investor information on CVB Financial Corp., visit our Citizens Business Bank website at www.cbbank.com and click on the “Investors” tab.
